title: How Uber Uses AI to Move from Java to Kotlin
summary: Uber's Ty Smith describes using AI to generate deterministic OpenRewrite-style recipes for Java-to-Kotlin migration with humans in the loop, and discusses review load, quality gates and how engineering roles may shift.

assertions.quote: people really only spend a small percentage of every day writing code. So just investing in one specific area, it's not going to

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: it's easy to do uh like the quick prototype with this type of tooling, but it's really hard to productionize something safely

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.

assertions.quote: generate those recipes and other tools with AI itself and have a human in the loop that can work in that system

verdicts.note: Migration case studies (Google, Amazon Java upgrades, Airbnb) got their scale from pairing LLMs with deterministic tooling and validation rather than free-form generation.

assertions.quote: you're holding that code to the same bar that you would hold a human to

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.

assertions.quote: it is a real concern if teams get too much uh code to review that things just stall

verdicts.note: The SmartBear/Cisco review study found defect detection drops beyond ~200-400 LOC per session; AI makes large PRs cheap to produce.

assertions.quote: it's about small reviewable diffs that um humans can review

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: I don't fall into the camp of thinking we'll all be without a job and replaced by AI, at least in the immediate future

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.

assertions.quote: they still need the fundamentals because all the code that's being produced they need to be able to critique it properly

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.

assertions.quote: that is probably going to need more and more people with a product mindset

verdicts.note: Plausible economic logic and widely argued, but not measured; execution, distribution and maintenance still matter.

assertions.quote: he was calling them the leader of the quarter because things are moving so quickly

verdicts.note: Tool-use and long-horizon capability jumps in 2025 changed effective workflows (chat-with-RAG to agentic loops); consistent with practitioner reports.

assertions.quote: engineers can do toil work, maybe a library upgrade or handling a deprecation or fixing a flaky test um with some of the agentic AIs

verdicts.note: Background agents do produce usable PRs for well-scoped chores, but merge rates vary widely and many PRs need iteration; 'most of the time' is optimistic.
